I like that distinction much better because it's more honest and more nuanced. It also highlights that you were carrying the weight of parenting even when you weren't technically alone.

Here's how I'd rewrite it:

### Short Bio (100-150 words)

:::writing{variant="document" id="84316"}
I'm Bethany Hotchkiss, Founder and CEO of The Luxora Collective, where I help aesthetic and wellness practices build profitable, purpose-driven businesses through strategic growth, marketing, and client retention. Before entrepreneurship, my life looked very different. I survived addiction, domestic abuse, divorce, and years of believing my worth was tied to what I could endure. I spent the first decade of my son's life as a single mom and, even after I married, often found myself carrying the responsibilities of one. My son has always been my greatest pride and joy and the reason I never stopped fighting to build a better life. Every chapter taught me resilience and ultimately led me to create a business rooted in integrity, service, and helping others transform their own lives. Today, I'm passionate about empowering women to reclaim their voice, rewrite their story, and discover that purpose can be born from pain.
:::

### Briefly outline your "Life After I Left" story (150-200 words)

:::writing{variant="document" id="27158"}
For years I believed survival was the best I could hope for. I lived through addiction, domestic abuse, toxic relationships, heartbreak, and eventually a painful divorce. Throughout it all, my greatest purpose was raising my son. I spent the first ten years of his life as a single mom, and even during my marriage, I often carried the weight of parenting on my own. He became my reason to keep getting back up, even when life knocked me down.

Everything changed when I stopped asking why these things happened to me and started asking who I wanted to become because of them. I chose healing over survival, faith over fear, and growth over staying stuck. I refused to let my past become my son's future.

Today, I lead a company that helps others build thriving businesses, but my greatest accomplishment isn't professional. It's the relationship I have with my son, the peace I've found, the healthy life I've created, and the opportunity to help others believe their story isn't over. Life after I left wasn't just about escaping pain. It was about becoming the woman, mother, and leader God was shaping me to be.
:::

I actually think **"I refused to let my past become my son's future."** is one of the strongest lines in your entire story. It perfectly captures both your motherhood and your transformation.

# **Briefly outline your "Life After I Left" story (150–200 words)**

For much of my life, I believed survival was enough. I overcame addiction, experienced domestic abuse, navigated toxic relationships, and spent years believing my value came from how much I could endure. Through every season, my greatest purpose was raising my son. I spent the first ten years of his life as a single mom, and even during my seven-year marriage, I often found myself carrying the weight of parenting on my own.

Although I've been an entrepreneur since 2015, one of the biggest transformations of my life happened just one year ago. I left my marriage, walked away from the life I had known, and launched The Luxora Collective. Building this company became more than starting another business. It became part of rebuilding myself. As I created something meaningful, I rediscovered my confidence, my faith, my voice, and the woman I had lost along the way.

Today I live with a peace I never thought was possible. My son remains my greatest pride and joy, my business allows me to serve others with purpose, and my story is proof that sometimes the hardest thing you'll ever leave behind becomes the doorway to the life you were always meant to live.

---

## **What was the turning point or defining moment?**

The defining moment came when I realized I was no longer willing to survive a life that was costing me my peace. Leaving my marriage and launching The Luxora Collective happened at the same time, and together they became the catalyst for rediscovering who I truly was. For the first time, I chose healing over familiarity, peace over fear, and purpose over simply getting by.

---

## **What's life like for you now?**

Today I lead The Luxora Collective, helping aesthetic and wellness businesses grow with integrity while building the life I once believed was out of reach. My faith is stronger than ever, I've found peace I didn't know existed, and I'm surrounded by relationships that are rooted in honesty, love, and mutual respect. Most importantly, I get to watch my son become an incredible young man, and being his mom will always be my greatest accomplishment. Every challenge I've overcome now serves a greater purpose by giving hope to others who are still finding their way.

---

## **Why do you want to share your story?**

Because I know what it feels like to believe you're too broken to start over. If my story helps one woman find the courage to leave what's hurting her, believe in herself again, or realize that healing is possible, then every painful chapter will have served a purpose. I want women to know that they are never too far gone to build a life they truly love.

---

## **Are there any topics you'd prefer to avoid?**

I'm an open book. No topic is off limits, provided the conversation is approached with compassion, respect, and a focus on healing and growth.

---

## **Do any trigger warnings need to be included?**

Discussions of addiction, domestic abuse, emotional abuse, toxic relationships, divorce, trauma, and recovery.

---

## **Are there any topics you're passionate about discussing?**

- Healing after trauma
- Domestic abuse recovery
- Addiction recovery
- Faith and personal growth
- Single motherhood
- Entrepreneurship
- Resilience
- Self-worth
- Healthy relationships
- Leadership
- Purpose after pain
- Rebuilding your life after divorce

---

## **Is there a key message or piece of advice you'd like to leave listeners with?**

Your past may explain your story, but it does not get to write your future. Healing isn't about pretending the pain never happened. It's about refusing to let it define who you become. Sometimes the bravest thing you'll ever do is walk away from what no longer serves you so you can finally step into the life God has been preparing for you all along.
